Six fae in scarlet petal-silk strung along an overhanging alder root, legs dangling, three screaming at the hull below and one already dangling by one knee having bet her hazelnut stake on the wrong boat entirely, a water-vole watching from the root-end with its paws folded.

A knot of fae in moss-velvet crowded onto a mossy boulder mid-stream, two holding a third by the ankles as she leans screaming over the drop, a fat frog sitting steady below absorbing the noise, one fae quietly moving pebbles along a twig to count hulls through.

Fae in marigold leaf-cloth running flat out along the low bank-root keeping level with the leaders, one already waist-deep and laughing, a second wringing out her soaked grass-cord sash as she runs, a kingfisher on the far stone watching the whole spectacle for its own reasons.

Four fae in woven grass perched on a beached oak leaf wide as the whole gravel spit, all facing the wrong bend and cheering a hull already swamped, one fae on a frog's back paddling hard into the current for a better view.

A loose diagonal of dragonflies flying escort above the field, each carrying one fae in plum petal-silk clutching the thorax with both fists, the rearmost fae leaning sideways at a dangerous angle to shout something back at the bank.

Seven fae in berry-red moss-velvet strung out along a fallen branch crossing the whole channel, one lying flat reaching a fern frond down to fend a hull off a stone, a snail making steady progress along the branch toward the far bank and winning.

Fae in birch-bark cloaks crowded into the fork of a bankside root above the first bend, two betting hazelnuts into an upturned acorn cap, one shouting corrections nobody asked for, a newt hanging motionless in the water below watching the same bend for different reasons.

Three fae in copper-thread grass-weave riding the backs of frogs in the shallows, leaning forward with their wings fanned for balance, one frog making a sudden lunge at a mayfly and nearly tipping its rider headfirst into the stream.

A row of fae in cream petal-silk lying flat on a low fern frond overhanging the whole channel, arms dangling, two of them dropping clover petals onto passing hulls for luck, one fae hanging entirely upside-down by her knees and losing a leaf-cloth shoe into the current.

Up in a tall fern above the bank, eight fae in moss-velvet and leaf-cloth jostling for position on a single frond, the frond bowing terrifyingly, one fae pressed against the stem holding everyone else's hazelnuts for safekeeping while chaos builds behind her.

A single fae in scarlet petal-silk balanced on a lone river pebble standing in mid-channel like a grey cliff above the fleet, arms wheeling, clearly about to fall, a dragonfly hovering at eye level as though deciding whether to catch her.

Fae in woven-grass tunics packed onto a broad floating oak leaf drifting slowly downstream, most of them shouting upstream at a race already past, one bailing the leaf with an acorn cap as water ships quietly over the stern edge.

Along the near bank a straggle of fae in plum and marigold petal-silk waving both arms at once, one sliding down the clay bank on a moss patch and arriving in the water still cheering, a water-vole hauled up on a root regarding her without pity.

Four fae in leaf-cloth perched on a watercress strand crossing the channel like a low bridge, bouncing, one tipping backward off it with a shriek and grabbing an ankle at the last moment, a duckling passing underneath with vast indifference.

Fae in moss-velvet clustered on a half-submerged root, two holding a fern frond up over themselves like a sunshade, a third with her ear pressed to the water listening for hull-sound, a fat frog below sitting perfectly still through all of it.

A kingfisher on the tip of a fallen willow branch over the far bend, utterly still, and under it twelve fae in scarlet and copper leaf-cloth running the branch's length, shaking it badly, oblivious to the kingfisher's contempt.

Six fae in birch-bark cloaks and petal-silk riding dragonfly escort in a tight ring above the leaders, one losing her grip and swinging by one hand beneath a wing, her moss-velvet hat spiralling down into the wake below.

Fae in cream and berry-red grass-weave pressed along the underside of an overhanging root, clinging like bats, all craning necks to watch upside-down, one dropping a hazelnut bet that lands precisely in a passing hull and is immediately claimed as ballast.

Three fae in marigold petal-silk standing on a single floating acorn cap in the shallows, the cap shipping water fast, two bailing and one still betting pebbles on the outcome, a newt nosing the cap's rim with scientific interest.

A heron motionless over the far bend like a grey cliff with ideas, and below it along the bank four fae in moss-velvet have tied a strand of plaited grass between two reeds and are arguing furiously about whether the lead hull crossed it first.

Eight fae in leaf-cloth packed onto a mossy boulder mid-stream, one holding up a fern frond to shade her eyes and giving everyone else wrong information, a second fae already in the water behind the boulder where the bank gave way under her boots of acorn-bark.

Fae in woven-grass and petal-silk running along the low root level with the bend, one pressing a polished pebble into another's hand as a losing bet paid mid-sprint without breaking stride, a water-vole watching from further along, unmoved.

Two fae in moss-velvet crouched on a half-submerged stone in the middle of the shallows, one reaching a fern frond out to fend a hull off the stone and accidentally fending it into the lead, the other covering her eyes with her leaf-cloth sleeve.

A loose crowd of fae in scarlet and plum petal-silk up in the fern bank above the course, some lying on their fronts at the frond edge, some swinging their legs, one fae lying on her back watching the sky, having bet on the first hull to swamp.

Fae in birch-bark and moss-velvet clustered on a fallen branch that grazes the water's surface, legs trailing in the current, one fae dragged slowly off the end by the flow still clutching a hazelnut, a dragonfly landing where she sat immediately after.

Six fae in petal-silk crowded onto a mossy boulder mid-stream, four leaning out screaming at the leading hull, one holding ankles, one already sliding in — a fat frog below them sitting steady, watching the turn, unbothered, a single hazelnut rolling off the boulder as ballast for a bet.

A line of fae in leaf-cloth sprinting flat out along the overhanging root, keeping level with the second boat, one waist-deep and still running, another waving a fern frond wildly at the wrong hull — a water-vole hauled up on a knob of root, paws folded, judging everyone.

Seven fae in moss-velvet strung along a fallen branch crossing the whole channel, legs swinging over the water, one lying flat reaching down with a dock-leaf to fend a hull off the stones — the kingfisher on the far branch-end watching the stream for its own separate hunger.

A knot of fae in birch-bark cloaks crowded on a great oak leaf beached on the gravel spit, all cheering a boat three lengths behind the leader, one small fae in marigold petal-silk on a frog's back paddling out into the channel for a closer look.

Four fae in grass-woven tunics up in a curling fern above the bank, legs dangling, betting hazelnuts into a heaped acorn cap, the tallest leaning so far out that the fern tips and drops him into the reeds — a dragonfly hovering exactly at fae-face height, watching.

Three fae in scarlet petal-silk riding frogs in the shallows, each frog lurching forward as its rider kicks its flanks, one fae already backward-facing having slid round on the lurch — a newt below the surface tracking the whole procession with one amber eye.

A straggle of fae in plum leaf-cloth running along the low bank, one wringing out a soaked moss-velvet cape where the mud gave way, two more holding a dock-leaf between them like a sail to catch a hull's bow-wave — a duckling overtaking all of them.

Five fae in woven-grass cloaks perched along a low root that trails into the water, the root bowing under the weight, the two farthest already ankle-deep and refusing to move — a water-vole swimming slow circles beneath them, unbothered by the shouting above.

Two fae in cream petal-silk up on a grey river pebble standing over the fleet like a small hill, waving both arms in opposite directions at different boats, a third fae on the pebble's far side counting the hulls through by moving hawthorn berries one at a time along a twig.

A dozen fae in copper-dyed birch-bark and moss-velvet packed onto a single fallen oak leaf drifting past as wide as three boats, half facing backwards, one standing on the curled edge which dips and ships water — a snail on the leaf's stem, travelling the whole course at its own pace and currently winning.

Six fae in berry-red leaf-cloth hanging from a low willow root over the water, gripping with knees and one hand each, free hands waving frantically, one dropping a wager-hazelnut that vanishes into the current — a kingfisher on the bank below watching the nut sink with great professional interest.

Four fae in petal-silk of marigold and plum running along the bank holding a strand of linked clover heads between them trying to stretch it across the channel to mark the far turn — a heron standing motionless over the bend, enormous above the whole straining effort.

Seven fae in moss-velvet crouched on a submerged stone just breaking the surface, water pouring over their feet, the shortest one in up to the hip and refusing all help, all of them shouting advice at a hull already past — a dragonfly keeping tight escort above them.

A fae in scarlet petal-silk lying full-length on a wet bank-stone, arm in the water up to the shoulder, trying to retrieve a wager-pebble that rolled in — three more in leaf-cloth standing over her offering loud contradictory directions, a fat frog watching from two inches away.

Five fae in woven-grass tunics packed onto a toadstool at the water's edge, the toadstool's rim cracking under the outside two, who have not noticed — one fae holds a bulrush stem high as a marker pole, a single dragonfly riding the top of it like a pennant.

A row of fae in birch-bark cloaks and petal-silk balanced along a reed stem arching over the water, the reed bending in a slow curve toward the surface under their weight, the fae at the lowest point trailing both feet in the current and still betting hazelnuts.

Three fae in plum petal-silk on a fern high above the bank, the fern springing under each step, one bouncing so hard she launches clear of the frond and catches the next one — a water-vole on the bank below watching upward with an expression of sustained alarm.

Eight fae in moss-velvet and marigold petal-silk crowded onto a mossy root-end jutting over a gravel bar, four leaning out over nothing, a fifth holding a twig to catch a hull that got trapped in the eddy — a newt resting on the gravel below, watching the hull spin.

A lone fae in berry-red leaf-cloth standing on a lily pad in the shallows, stamping one foot to make the pad rock and send a small wave into the channel at the passing hulls — the fat frog whose pad it is has not moved, but its expression has changed.

Six fae in cream petal-silk and woven-grass cloaks running in a mob along the far bank, one tripping over a root and rolling, coming up still shouting — a duckling pacing them from the water, matching speed, pulling ahead on the straight with visible ease.

Four fae in scarlet and copper petal-silk hanging upside-down from a low branch over the water, knees hooked on bark, hair streaming, passing hazelnuts and river pebbles between them as changing bets — a dragonfly flying slow figures-of-eight below their heads, exactly at nose height.

A fae in moss-velvet standing on a frog's back in midstream, one arm out for balance, the other holding a fern frond high to signal the count — the frog swimming steadily forward through the whole contest, carrying the fae ten lengths past the intended station before stopping.

Five fae in plum and marigold leaf-cloth wedged into the fork of an alder root above the waterline, two facing each other in furious argument over a bet of three hazelnuts and one pebble, the other three ignoring them and watching the race with total absorption.

Three fae in birch-bark and grass-cord perched on the back of a water-vole in the shallows, the vole swimming forward anyway, undeterred — one fae has slipped and is trailing behind gripping a fistful of the vole's fur, still commentating on the race to anyone within earshot.

Seven fae in berry-red and cream petal-silk strung along a watercress strand crossing the channel like a low bridge, bouncing on it, one who bounced too hard dangling with both hands in the current — a mayfly the size of a fae rising from the water just underneath, ignoring everything.

A fae in scarlet petal-silk sprinting along the bank with an acorn-cap full of river pebbles, counting them out one at a time as each hull passes, running out of pebbles with two hulls still to come — a snail on the bankstone beside her, keeping meticulous pace.

Five fae in woven-grass and moss-velvet crammed onto the broad back of a grey river pebble standing over the fleet like a small hill, the one on the very top using a bulrush stem as a tall signalling wand — a kingfisher perched on the wand's tip, unasked.

Four fae in marigold petal-silk and leaf-cloth up in the reeds, one per stem, each reed swaying a different direction in the wash of the passing hulls, the fae gripping with both knees and still finding a free hand to wave — a dragonfly weaving between them at speed.

A mob of fae in plum and copper petal-silk on a fallen branch that crosses the water, one fae belly-flat reaching a fern frond to save a hull from the stones, the hull ramming the frond sideways — the fae sliding two inches forward but holding on, triumphant.

Six fae in birch-bark cloaks and scarlet petal-silk on a great dock-leaf beached on the gravel, all bet on the same boat, which is currently spinning backwards in an eddy — one stands with arms folded watching it spin, one has sat down in grief, one is laughing.

Six fae in scarlet petal-silk strung along an overhanging alder root, legs dangling, three screaming at the leading hull, one losing a hazelnut bet into the current, a water-vole below on a root-knob watching with its paws pressed together, its tail curled neat as a question.

A knot of fae in moss-velvet riding the backs of three frogs in the shallows, spurring their mounts forward to keep pace, one fae sliding sideways off a slick green flank, shrieking, still pointing at the boats, a mayfly the size of a rowing fae hovering above them all.

Two dozen fae in leaf-cloth and woven-grass sashes crowded onto a beached oak leaf wide as three boats, all facing the wrong bend, cheering wildly for a hull already out of the running, a snail at the leaf's prow keeping its own slow purposeful pace along the bank.

A line of fae in plum petal-silk running flat out along the low bank root, keeping level with the second hull, one already shin-deep in the current and laughing, one holding a fern frond over the water like a roof, a single bulrush rising taller than any mast above them.

Five fae in birch-bark tunics perched along a fallen branch spanning the full channel, one lying flat reaching down with a twig to nudge a wayward hull, a kingfisher on the far branch-end watching the whole fleet for reasons entirely its own.

A crowd of fae in marigold petal-silk packed onto a mossy boulder mid-stream, four leaning out over the drop with a fifth holding their ankles, shouting competing directions, a fat frog sitting perfectly still on the boulder's wet toe watching the turn with sovereign indifference.

Seven fae in moss-velvet up in a broad fern above the bank, each clutching a fern finger for balance, two shaking hazelnuts and pebbles into an acorn-cap betting pool, one hanging half-off a frond to see past the watercress crossing the channel like a low bridge below.

Three fae in cream petal-silk dangling from a low willow-hair root over the shallows, toes grazing the surface, using their free hands to splash a rival crew's wake back at them, a newt in the murk below pausing mid-step to watch one sandal fall and sink.

A thin straggle of fae in copper-dyed leaf-cloth jogging along the gravel spit, one wringing a soaked skirt as the bank crumbled, one using a dandelion stalk as a pointing rod to call a boat home, a duckling drifting through the middle of the whole argument, unconcerned.

Four fae in berry-red petal-silk balanced on a single river pebble standing over the fleet like a grey boulder, all four arms out for balance, one tumbling off the back into the stream, a dragonfly hovering exactly at their eye level, wings a copper blur.

A long row of fae in woven-grass tunics draped over the curved flank of a waterlogged root, each betting a pebble by pressing it along a twig toward the leader's end, the twig already tipping, one fae on the lowest curve up to her waist in cold water still voting.

Six fae in moss-velvet clinging to the underside of a broad fern frond that overhangs the whole racing field like a roof, watching upside-down, their pointed ears tilting every time a hull passes below, a single acorn cup shipping enough water to swamp a hull rolling past them.

A pair of fae in leaf-cloth stationed on opposite banks of the channel, leaning so far toward each other over the stream they are nearly touching, passing a hazelnut bet hand to hand across the gap, a kingfisher on a twig above them pretending not to see.

Eight fae in scarlet and gold petal-silk running along the top of a grassy bank, one tripping over a root and completing a full roll back to standing without stopping the shouting, a frog on the bank below watching the roll with both eyes independently tracking.

Three fae in plum moss-velvet riding a slow water-vole through the margins, two pointing the animal toward the inside bend for a better view, one braiding its fur with a grass cord while it swims, the water-vole aiming steadily for a reed clump regardless.

A single fae in birch-bark and woven grass lying flat on the jutting end of a branch over the stream, counting boats through by moving river pebbles along the bark with one finger, a dragonfly landing on the pebble pile and refusing to move, disrupting the count entirely.

Five fae in marigold petal-silk packed onto the broad cap of a chanterelle at the bank's edge, the cap bending lower with each cheer, two already holding on with both hands as it tips, a snail alongside on the stem watching its property threatened with visible alarm.

A gang of fae in leaf-cloth and moss-velvet betting hazelnuts into a hollowed acorn cap on top of a lichen boulder, one fae appointed to hold the stakes eating a hazelnut mid-argument, caught, holding the half-eaten nut behind their back with elaborate innocence.

Seven fae in deep berry-red petal-silk hung along a strand of grass-cord strung between two reeds, swinging their legs over the fleet, one whose reed gave way mid-race now standing waist-deep below, still cheering, still holding their hazelnut above the waterline.

A cluster of fae in woven-reed tunics crowded onto a lily pad in the slack water, their combined weight making it list, one bailing the pooling water with an acorn cap, two still waving fern-tip banners at a boat that passed four lengths ago.

Two fae in cream petal-silk standing on the back of a single large frog mid-stream, one using a curved reed as a speaking-tube toward the bank, the frog's expression suggesting this was agreed to for one lap only and that lap has concluded.

A dozen fae in copper leaf-cloth sprinting along a fallen log parallel to the channel, legs pumping, one losing both shoes, retrieving one shoe, abandoning the other with grief and continuing, a water-vole watching from below the log with its nose working rapidly.

Three fae in moss-velvet up a bulrush, wound around the stem at different heights, calling down results to a fourth on the bank who is writing nothing down because there is nothing to write on and the system is already failing, a newt motionless at the bank's edge.

Six fae in plum and scarlet petal-silk crowded onto a gravel spit, three facing each other in violent disagreement over which hull leads, one pointing at a floating oak leaf drifting past wide as three boats as definitive evidence of something, a duckling paddling through the debate.

A line of fae in marigold woven-grass cloaks hanging by their knees from a low root above the water, watching the race upside-down, faces very red, one whose ankle-grip failed already in the stream below looking back up at the others with dignified calm.

Four fae in leaf-cloth on a mossy stone mid-stream, three having turned their backs on the race to settle a hazelnut argument, one facing forward in lonely rapture watching a dragonfly fly escort above the leading hull, both of them the only ones paying attention.

A fae in deep moss-velvet perched alone on the point of a branch tip above the channel, swaying with every gust, using a stripped willow-hair to lash herself on, holding a fern frond out to fend a hull off the stones, a kingfisher watching from two arm-lengths away.

Eight fae in berry-red petal-silk and grass-woven belts jostling along the bank's root-ladder, one fallen in pulling a second in pulling a third, the fourth holding the fifth's ankles, the sixth cheering, the seventh helping, the eighth already dry again and betting, a frog witnessing the full chain.

A scatter of fae in birch-bark capes high in a fern above the channel, each on their own frond, all leaning inward over the water at different angles like a broken fence, one frond already bending toward the stream below, its rider still refusing to climb back.

Five fae in copper and cream petal-silk seated in a solemn row on a waterlogged root, performing the most restrained possible appreciation of the whole event, one secretly passing a hazelnut bet along the line behind their backs, a newt on the root below watching the transaction from the start.

Six fae in scarlet petal-silk crowded onto a half-submerged alder root, four shaking fern fronds wildly at the leaders, one already chest-deep having slid off, a seventh fae in moss-velvet quietly winning every hazelnut bet stacked in an acorn cap beside her.

A knot of fae in plum leaf-cloth strung along an overhanging willow root, legs dangling, all leaning the same direction at once so the root bows and creaks, a water-vole below on a stone with its paws folded, entirely unimpressed.

Three fae in marigold petal-silk riding frogs through the shallows, trying to keep pace with the fleet, their mounts veering badly, one frog having turned completely around, the fae aboard her waving and cheering a boat already a full oak-leaf-length behind.

A long diagonal of dragonflies flying escort just above the channel, each one shadowing a hull, and up in the broad fern above the bank a lone fae in moss-velvet lying flat watching through a gap in the fronds, one hand gripping a spare rowanberry for no clear reason.

Fae in woven-grass tunics packed onto a great beached oak leaf on the gravel spit, all facing the bend the boats have already rounded, one climbing another's shoulders to see over, a newt threading between their feet without once being noticed.

Two fae in berry-red moss-velvet out along a fallen branch crossing the full width of the channel, one reaching down with a fern frond to fend a hull clear of the bark, the kingfisher on the branch-end watching the fish and ignoring the race entirely.

A row of fae in cream petal-silk running flat along the low bank, arms pumping, one already tumbled into the mud laughing, a second stopping to wring her leaf-cloth hem, a fat frog sitting steady on the nearest lily pad watching the turn they are all missing.

Four fae in copper-threaded leaf-cloth betting hazelnuts into a heap on a mossy boulder mid-stream, a fifth fae in scarlet arriving breathless to bet the single polished river pebble she carries, and a snail making steady progress around the boulder's base, already halfway.

A cluster of fae in plum and moss-velvet up in a tall fern above the bank, clinging to the stems, the whole frond bowing under them until the tip nearly brushes the water, one fae at the very end reaching out with both arms and finding nothing to touch.

Fae in marigold leaf-cloth crowded onto the broad back of a mossy mid-stream boulder, three pounding the stone with fern-stem drumsticks in a wild rhythm, a fourth holding a dragonfly's tail to stop it leaving, the dragonfly hovering in place and looking annoyed.

A single fae in scarlet petal-silk lying belly-down on a root above the far bend, one hand trailing in the water holding a pebble she is moving along a twig to count the hulls through, a duckling drifting under her arm as though this is normal.

Seven fae in woven-grass and birch-bark tunics sitting out along a low root in a line, each holding the waist of the one in front, the front fae leaning so far out over the dark water that her pointed ears nearly touch the surface.

Fae in moss-velvet on both banks straining toward each other across the channel, the gap too wide, one tossing a hazelnut across as a bet to a catcher who fumbles it into the current, a mayfly lifting past them both unhurried and huge as a fae.

A fae in berry-red leaf-cloth standing upright on a frog's back in the shallows, arms raised, shouting at the leading hull, the frog inching forward into the channel entirely on its own authority, both of them now further out than intended.

Three fae in plum petal-silk clinging to the high inside bend of a root arch, completely upside-down above the water, cheering at the boats below them, one losing a woven-grass sandal that falls and lands perfectly in an empty acorn cap floating past.
